statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low while event and geopolitical Stress is extreme.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains below the block threshold; the 12:30–14:00 UTC sequence is the main conditional checkpoint.
headline: Low Tail, extreme Stress into the U.S. event cluster
body: Delayed NQ remains near flat within a broad two-sided session range. Mixed index futures and firmer bond futures conflict with stronger oil and broad semiconductor weakness, while the 12:30 UTC data/Waller cluster and 14:00 UTC ISM keep Stress extreme.

lookbackSummary: Published Tail moved from elevated/watch during part of the prior U.S. session to low overnight and through the European morning. The September 2 22:00 UTC slot remains unavailable.
outlookSummary: Conditional Tail reaches WATCH around the 12:30 UTC data/Waller cluster, the U.S. cash-open transition and the 14:00 UTC ISM release. A blocking state still requires subsequently observed persistent NQ extension and poor retracement quality; Friday payroll proximity mainly sustains Stress.

forecast.analysis: Delayed NQ remains near flat inside the session range; index futures are mixed, bond futures firmer, oil higher and semiconductors broadly weaker. The 12:30 UTC cluster is imminent, so Stress is extreme while Tail remains low.
drivers: Delayed NQ remains inside the session range

forecast.analysis: After the 12:30 releases, WATCH applies only if NQ keeps extending with shallow or failed pullbacks into the 13:30 cash open; orderly two-way discovery would argue lower Tail.
ISM at 14:00 UTC is a second information wave. WATCH is conditional on repeated directional extension and weak retracements; a fast two-sided response would keep Tail below the block threshold.
During the first full post-ISM hour, WATCH depends on whether any directional move survives counter-swings. Meaningful retracements or fading cross-asset alignment would reduce Tail.
If event repricing is being absorbed through meaningful pullbacks, Tail falls back below WATCH while Stress remains extreme because oil, rates and Friday payroll risk are still active.
Mid-session Tail stays low if rotation remains two-sided. A new persistent leg would require confirmation from yields, volatility, semiconductors or megacaps before materially changing the path.
Late-afternoon Tail remains low if extensions continue to retrace. A one-way second leg with price holding near a session extreme would be the main escalation condition.
Hammack's scheduled remarks are a medium checkpoint. Tail remains low unless the remarks coincide with continued directional extension and failed pullbacks rather than short-lived volatility.
After the speaker window, orderly rotation would keep Tail low even if Stress stays extreme. A persistent cross-asset move would be the condition for renewed WATCH risk.
Into the U.S. cash close, fading directional efficiency keeps Tail low. A close pinned near an extreme after repeated failed retracements would be the main contrary signal.
Post-cash liquidity can magnify short moves, but Tail stays low unless thin trading produces sustained extension without meaningful retracement.
Early overnight Tail stays low unless a fresh geopolitical or policy catalyst creates a sustained directional path. Friday payroll proximity mainly keeps Stress elevated.
During early Asia, Tail remains low if price discovery is two-sided. A geopolitical discontinuity or aligned oil-yield-equity move would be the main conditional amplifier.
Overnight structure remains the key test: retraced moves support low Tail, while persistent extension across successive liquidity windows would raise concern.
Later Asia keeps low Tail under a reverting path. Sustained energy and rates pressure aligned with one-way NQ would be needed for a materially higher reading.
At the Asia-Europe transition, liquidity rises and headline sensitivity can increase. Tail stays low unless pullbacks become persistently shallow through the handoff.
European participation increases depth. Two-sided price discovery would keep Tail low, while repeated extension through failed retracements would be the escalation signal.
As Europe matures, Friday payroll proximity raises Stress more than Tail. Low Tail persists if directional moves continue to retrace.
Pre-U.S. positioning becomes more relevant. Tail stays low if NQ moves remain rotational; holding near an overnight extreme with aligned cross-assets would raise the conditional path.
U.S. premarket liquidity begins to matter more. Tail remains low unless a directional move develops shallow pullbacks and repeated extension ahead of payrolls.
Four-plus hours before payrolls, event sensitivity raises Stress without assuming a release outcome. Tail stays low while price action remains two-sided.
Pre-release positioning can thin liquidity and increase whipsaw risk. Tail remains below WATCH unless directional efficiency rises and retracements weaken.
Approaching the final pre-payroll hours, conditional Tail reaches WATCH because liquidity and positioning can become fragile; this does not assume any release result or future market reaction.

Roughly 90 minutes before the scheduled employment report, WATCH reflects event proximity and potential liquidity imbalance only. A blocking state still requires subsequently observed persistent extension.

Post-ISM WATCH persists only if one-way structure survives counter-swings.
